Smt.P.Lakshminarasamma, Wife of Late Padmanabha Rao, 2 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 Aged about 75 years, All are residing at Behind Municipal Office, 21st Ward, Bagepalli, Chikkaballapura District, Pin-561 207. (By Pleader Shri K.Prakash) Common Judgment The petitioners have filed these respective claim petitions in Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 as against the 3 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 respondents U/S. 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- and Rs.80,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in Mvc 7423/2018 death of P.Narahari Rao, Son of Padmanabha Rao and in a road traffic accident. 2. All these petitions are arising out of the same accident, hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common discussion. 3. The brief contents of both the petitions are as In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 2 under: The allegation of the petitioners is that, on 28.11.2018 at about 10.00 a.m. the petitioner in Mvc 7423/2018 was riding the Honda Splendar motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-L-1157 along with pillion rider by name P.Narahari Rao from Bagepalli towards Somenahalli on the extreme left side on Nh-7 road slowly, cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations at that time the driver of the Tractor bearing No.KA-40-TA-5425 and trailer bearing No.KA- 40-T-6965 came from opposite direction with high speed in a 4 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others dashed against the Honda Splendor and again wheel of the Engine Tractor ran on the chest of the pillion rider P.Narahari Rao and he succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital. Due to the impact, the petitioner in Mvc 7423/2018 sustained grievous injuries. Immediately he was shifted to Bagepalli Government hospital, wherein first aid treatment and then referred to Chikkaballapura Government hospital, wherein he took the conservative treatment and again referred to Jeevan Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took the treatment as inpatient. 4. The contention of the petitioners in Mvc No.7423/2018 is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 44 years, Fda in Beo Office in In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 3 Gudibande and earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, he could not do the work as earlier. 5. The contention of the petitioner in Mvc No.7424/2018 is that, deceased was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 55 years, Gazette Manager at Beo office 5 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 and earning a sum of Rs.60,000/- per month. Due to the said demise of the Narahari Rao the petitioners have put into deep mental shock and agony. P.Narahari Rao was contributing the entire income to the family members. 6. The contention of the petitioners is that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor Engine bearing NoKA-40-TA-5425 and trailer bearing No.KA-40-T-6965. So, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners. Contending the above facts, the petitioners have filed these respective claim petitions and prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 7. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and filed their written statement. 8. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 in both the cases are as under: The contention of the respondent No.1 is that, petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 4 6 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner only and not on the part of the driver of the tractor. Further contended that this respondent got insured his vehicle Tractor Engine bearing No.KA-40-TA-5425, trailer bearing No.KA-40-T-6965 with respondent No.2 and the policy was in force at that time. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioners as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss both the claim petitions with cost. 9. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 in both the cases are as under: The contention of the respondent No.2 is that, petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further this respondent has contended that it has issued policy bearing No.M3309095 against a tractor bearing Engine No.S3251G85214 and Chassis Mea 908A5Ag2075942 and valid from 1.10.2018 to 30.9.2019. Further contended that the said tractor attached with trailer bearing No.KA-40-T-6965 at the time of alleged accident. The said trailer bearing No.Ka-40-T-6965 was not insured with this respondent. The 7 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 Rc of the said trailer stands in the name of Shri Nagabhushan K., son of Late.Krishnappa Further contended that the petition In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 5 is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. Further contended that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the petitioner was riding the alleged motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-L-1157 without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmets and without possessing valid vehicle documents in a ash and negligent manner and suffered self accident. Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle. Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provision u/s 134(c) and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 6 Issues in Mvc 7424/2018 In order to prove their case, petitioner in Mvc 7423/2018 is examined as Pw1 and got marked The petitioner in Mvc 7423/2018 and petitioner No.1 in Mvc 7424/2018 are examined as Pw1 and Pw2. They have stated in their evidence by reiterating the contents of the petition. Further he argued that petitioners have proved their case by producing the oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly he prays to allow the petition. 18. Per contra the learned counsel for the respondents have argued that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-L-1157 and not on the part of the driver of the tractor bearing No.KA-40- Ta-5425. Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition. 20. On perusal of Ex.P2 complaint, it reveals that complaint has been lodged by Vasundahara, Wife of P.Narahari Rao on 28.11.2018. Based on the complaint, Fir at Ex.P1 has been registered by Bagepalli Police, in Cr.No.328/2018 against the driver of the tractor bearing No.KA-40-T-6965 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 304(A) of Ipc. are the spot mahazar and sketch reveals that the scene 12 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 of occurrence and it corroborates the evidence of Pw1. The counsel for the respondents have argued that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-L-1157 and not on the part of the driver of the tractor bearing No.KA-40-TA-5425. On the other hand, the petitioners have proved their case that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor engine bearing No.KA-40-TA-5425. 22. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of Mv Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 Sar (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 23. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses. On record he has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P8 to the extent of Rs.69,916/-. Further the petitioner has produced Ex.P28 statement of reimbursement of medical expenses. On perusal of the same, it shows that the petitioner has claimed Rs.75,962/- and he got reimbursement of Rs.60,146/- and remaining Rs.15,816/-. He has admitted in his cross-examination that remaining Rs.15,816/- he has paid cash. But on perusal of Ex.P8, the petitioner has produced bill to the extent of Rs.69,916/- and from his department he got reimbursement of Rs.56,532/- remaining Rs.13,384/- has paid by cash. The petitioner has not produced the 2nd bill. Therefore, it is just and proper to award Rs.13,384/- towards medical expenses. 17 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 29. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 44 years and working as Fda in Beo office, Gudibande. Due to the accidental injuries he cannot work as usual. The petitioner has not examined the competent doctor to speak about the grievousness or to assess permanent disability. So, no amount is granted under this head. 30. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. 38 . At this juncture this court has drawn the attention on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2017 Acj 2700 in between National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others. In the said decision, it is held that; Quantum---Fatal accident--- Principles of assessment---future prospects----Whether legal representatives of the deceased who was on fixed salary or self-employed or aged between 50 and 60 would be entitled to In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 16 benefit of future prospects for the purpose of computation of compensation---Held: yes; case-law discussed. So, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2012 Acj 1298 in between Sarlaverma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., if 4-6 dependants, 1/4th shall be deducted towards the personal and living expenses. In the case on hand, petitioners 1 to 4 are financial dependants of the deceased, so, 1/4th of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses, on such deduction, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.6,56,955/-p.a. comes to Rs.59,12,595/-. 42 . At this juncture I relied the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.9581/2018 (Arising out of Slp (Civil) No.3192/2018) in case of 24 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 Muama General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and Others. In which it is held in para No.8.7 that " A Constitution Bench of this Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) dealt with the various heads under which the compensation it so be awarded in a death case. One of these heads is "Loss of Consortium": In legal parlance "consortium" is a compendious term which encompasses 'spousal consortium; parental consortium In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 18 and filial consortium. The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family. With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse. Spousal consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband -wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of "company, society, co- operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation." 25 Scch-17 Mvc 7423/2018 & 7424/2018 Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training." Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child. An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased. is to lose their child during their lifetime. Modern jurisdictions world-over have recognized that the value of child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in case of death of a child. In Mvc Shri H.N. Raghu vs Shri H.S.Nagaraju on 9 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119717867/ 19 43. The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
